chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: New Orleans people share
summary: Milt says New Orleans is outgoing, and Danny says the poorest people share, which is why they survive.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: But Louis was really a natural. And he was really just so outgoing. And I guess that's part of New Orleans. There's something about this place that makes people like that. I'm just talking to you, and I know how you are, and I was just telling you about this lady who came up there and met my wife, and she said, 'Hi, I'm just calling to see how you're doing...'
She knew I'm on a diet, Mona had told her that I was on a diet, and she went ahead and she skinned the chicken, and ....[INAUDIBLE]...
Yeah, they share here, and that's very good.
The poorest people share. Is that right?
The same cats is all broke at the same time.
Well, I just wanted to get in there what you're doing. And I want to thank you very much for this opportunity to spend some time with you. More than even the interview, just being with you.
